findings.finding: The approach cites 16 pre-existing tests but does not state that they will be run, nor that each is independently tied to the exact current instruction text. A ledger citation alone can mask tests that assert an adjacent sentence, a stale copy, or a different document.

findings.finding: “Whitespace-normalized form” is underspecified. A broad normalizer can make meaningful textual edits—including punctuation, line joining, or markdown restructuring—pass while the governing instruction has materially changed.

findings.finding: Several pinned strings include markdown formatting tokens (``, backticks, section-heading `##` prefixes like `"## Step 7: Create PR (Optional)"`). Because the assertion runs against whitespace-normalized raw text, any purely cosmetic formatting change (heading level shift, bold removed) trips the test even though the governing instruction is unchanged. This is partially by design, but the self-review payload claims uniform whitespace normalization was applied to avoid non-semantic failures while these punctuation/format-sensitive pins reintroduce that brittleness.
findings.suggestion: Pin the prose sentence (or strip markdown emphasis before asserting) rather than formatting-decorated headings; keep one heading anchor per test at most.
